newsitem.title: UK: Czarnikow sees record sugar output in Brazil NNE.
newsitem.headline: Czarnikow sees record sugar output in Brazil NNE.

text.p: Brazil's north north-east (NNE) cane growing region could set a new sugar production record in 1996/97, exceeding last year's record of 3.54 million tonnes raw value, Czarnikow Sugar said in its monthly report on Thursday. Czarnikow said a few mills in the region had started crushing very promptly this season.
"Although no progress has yet been reported, early indications continue to bear out previous expectations that the new crop will be a very good one," the report said.
It added that the Brazilian government was still hesitating to remove a 40-percent tax on the remaining 20 percent of sugar set for export in this year's crop plan.
But NNE exports could soar once the tax was removed, as it already has been for most of the 1996/97 crop, it said.
"Export possibilities...remain somewhat sketchy as the trade is awaiting the lifting of the export tax on the remaining 20 percent of the export quota," Czarnikow said.
"Given the excellent prospects for the crop in the NNE, there might be a surge in the availability from this origin once the limits are revised," it said.
It added the quota was unlikely to be allocated before the expiry of New York's October futures contract.
